authority: European Patent Organisation / European Patent Convention (EPC)
title: EPC Article 52 - Patentable Inventions
text: EPC Article 52 Patentable inventions: (1) European patents shall be granted for any inventions, in all fields of technology, provided that they are new, involve an inventive step and are susceptible of industrial application. (2) The following in particular shall not be regarded as inventions: discoveries, scientific theories and mathematical methods; aesthetic creations; schemes, rules and methods for performing mental acts, playing games or doing business, and programs for computers; presentations of information.

authority: European Patent Organisation / European Patent Convention (EPC)
title: EPC Article 53(c) - Exceptions to Patentability (Methods for Treatment Exclusion)
text: EPC Article 53 Exceptions to patentability: European patents shall not be granted in respect of: (c) methods for treatment of the human or animal body by surgery or therapy and diagnostic methods practised on the human or animal body; this provision shall not apply to products, in particular substances or compositions, for use in any of these methods. Medical and therapeutic products, including herbal and pharmaceutical formulations, remain patentable as compositions.

authority: European Patent Organisation / European Patent Convention (EPC)
title: EPC Article 54 - Novelty and State of the Art Definition
text: EPC Article 54 Novelty: (1) An invention shall be considered to be new if it does not form part of the state of the art. (2) The state of the art shall be held to comprise everything made available to the public by means of a written or oral description, by use, or in any other way, before the date of filing of the European patent application. Novelty requires that no single prior art publication or disclosure reveals all features of the claimed formulation.

authority: European Patent Organisation / European Patent Convention (EPC)
title: EPC Article 54(5) - Second Medical Use and Purpose-Related Product Claims
text: EPC Article 54(5) Second Medical Use: Paragraphs 2 and 3 shall not exclude the patentability of any substance or composition referred to in paragraph 4 for any specific use in a method referred to in Article 53(c), provided that such use is not comprised in the state of the art. Under EPC Article 54(5), a known botanical compound or classical Ayurvedic herbal extract can be patented for a specific new therapeutic indication in the purpose-related product claim format: 'Substance X for use in the treatment of disease Y.'

authority: European Patent Organisation / European Patent Convention (EPC)
title: EPC Article 56 - Inventive Step and the Problem-Solution Approach
text: EPC Article 56 Inventive step: An invention shall be considered as involving an inventive step if, having regard to the state of the art, it is not obvious to a person skilled in the art. The EPO evaluates inventive step using the tripartite Problem-Solution Approach: (1) determine closest prior art, (2) establish technical effect and objective technical problem, (3) assess whether skilled person starting from closest prior art would have arrived at claimed composition without inventive effort. In polyherbal mixtures, unexpected synergistic technical effect is required to overcome an obviousness objection.

authority: European Patent Organisation / European Patent Convention (EPC)
title: EPC Article 57 - Industrial Applicability
text: EPC Article 57 Industrial application: An invention shall be considered as susceptible of industrial application if it can be made or used in any kind of industry, including agriculture. Herbal formulations manufactured by standardized extraction, blending, tableting, or pharmaceutical processing satisfy industrial applicability.

authority: European Patent Organisation / European Patent Convention (EPC)
title: EPC Article 83 - Sufficiency of Disclosure for Botanical Compositions
text: EPC Article 83 Disclosure of the invention: The European patent application shall disclose the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for it to be carried out by a person skilled in the art. For complex botanical extracts, herbal synergies, and biological compositions, the specification must provide reproducible extraction protocols, characterization parameters (HPLC/TLC fingerprinting, marker concentrations), and verifiable experimental synergy data to enable the skilled person to reproduce the claimed composition across the entire scope of the claims.

authority: European Patent Organisation / European Patent Convention (EPC)
title: EPC Article 64 & National Market Boundary - Patent Grant vs Pharmaceutical Marketing Authorization
text: EPC Article 64 Rights conferred by a European patent and Regulatory Boundary: A European patent confers on its proprietor from the date on which the mention of its grant is published in the European Patent Bulletin, in each Contracting State in respect of which it is granted, the same rights as would be conferred by a national patent granted in that State. CRITICAL REGULATORY BOUNDARY: An EPC patent grant is strictly a negative right of commercial exclusion and DOES NOT grant marketing authorization or regulatory permission to sell pharmaceutical or herbal medicinal products in any EU member state. Marketing authorization must be separately obtained through the European Medicines Agency (EMA) or national competent authorities under Directive 2001/83/EC or Directive 2004/24/EC.

authority: European Parliament and Council / European Union Pharmaceutical Law
title: Directive 2004/24/EC - Traditional Herbal Medicinal Products Directive (THMPD)
text: Directive 2004/24/EC amending Directive 2001/83/EC: Establishes a simplified registration procedure for traditional herbal medicinal products (THMP). To qualify for registration: (1) the medicinal product must contain exclusively herbal substances or preparations; (2) it must have been in traditional medicinal use throughout a period of at least 30 years preceding the date of application, including at least 15 years within the European Union / EEA; (3) safety data and plausible efficacy must be substantiated by bibliographical references or expert evidence; (4) full GMP compliance and pharmaceutical quality dossiers (CTD Module 3) are mandatory.
